latest.text:
Alcaraz beat Shelton in three sets in the SF in Turin to reach the final and he had to come from a set down to do it.

It was Shelton who made the better start. He broke for 2–0 and later came back from 15–40 on his own serve to keep that lead. He took the first set 6–3 and was one set away from the final. That early break stayed with Alcaraz. Alcaraz afterwards: "The break early (in the first set) was tough for me to deal with. But I’m happy that I came back in the second set playing such great tennis," He did not see another break point for the rest of the match.

The second set turned slowly his way. He got the break at 5–3 and took the set 6–3 for one set all. The deciding set was the closest part of the match. Neither player was broken, so it went to a tiebreak. There Alcaraz was clearly the better player and won it 7–1.

That steady serving carried him through a final set with no break and his serve was the base of it all. He held to love 6 times and won 73% of the points behind his second serve, far above his 56% average on hard.

So Alcaraz is through to the final, after a start that was tough for him to deal with and a comeback that he was happy with. He played great tennis when the match was closest and gave Shelton almost nothing on his serve. That made the difference in the end.

latest.text:
Medvedev beat Tiafoe 6–3, 6–4 in the group stage to pick up a win in his second group match in Turin. It was the first appearance of Tiafoe at this event.

The start was not easy for Medvedev. He was the first to come under pressure and had to save two break points. He held, broke soon after and took the first set 6–3. Tiafoe came out aggressive in the second set and showed fine touch near the net. Medvedev stayed calm, broke late in the set and served out the match. Whatever happens next, he enjoys being here: "The Finals is a great tournament because whenever you finish it is great because you have some rest at the end of the season. But if you continue playing that is great because I love to win, …" Today he got that win.

Medvedev was at his best when it mattered most. He saved every break point he faced and his defence kept Tiafoe chasing. His serve was the base of it, with 76% of first serves in against his 65% average on hard. The score stayed close only because Tiafoe saved most of the break points against him.

A win that says a lot about Medvedev's experience on this stage, against a player new to it. He won this event in London in 2020 and played like a man who knows it well. Up next: his last group match.
